To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) differential privacy is a good privacy definition, (ii) differential privacy is not incompatible with high utility, (iii) the utility of differentially private databases can be significantly improved by using the right algorithm, (iv) differential privacy is robust against a variety of attacks, (v) differential privacy is the first definition that can be implemented in a variety of settings, (vi) differential privacy is useful in settings other than databases, (vii) the definition of differential privacy is simple enough
differential privacy is the appropriate privacy definition for the statistical database problem, and that differential privacy is achievable with reasonable utility.

(i) differential privacy is a good definition of privacy; (ii) differential privacy can be achieved with a reasonable loss in utility (for example, a loss of 10% in accuracy); (iii) there are many applications in which the loss in utility is acceptable; (iv) the definition is strong enough to prevent the disclosure of sensitive information, even if the data analyst has access to other information about the individuals;
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: How can we release a database that is as informative as possible while still protecting the privacy of its constituents?
the following questions: How much can be said about the population as a as whole, given that the privacy of individuals is protected? What is the price of privacy?
the following questions: 1. What are the privacy goals of the data analyst, and what is the power of an adversary who wishes to compromise privacy?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, given a privacy goal and a utility goal, there is no known method to achieve both.
the privacy and utility goals of statistical databases are not compatible.
the privacy of individuals is preserved if no adversary with access to auxiliary data, and with the power to compromise privacy, can learn any information about the individuals in the database.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the privacy goals are not achievable, but that differential privacy is the closest we can get to the ideal.

we show how to use differential privacy to achieve privacy goals, while maintaining utility.
On the Difficultie...
we have defined a notion of privacy that we call differential privacy, and have shown that it can be achieved with very little loss in utility.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the privacy guarantees we can provide are very weak, and the utility of the resulting databases is also weak.
, in order to protect the privacy of individuals, it is necessary to sacrifice a significant amount of the utility of the database.
, in the presence of a moderately powerful adversary, it is difficult to prevent disclosure of any information whatsoever about individuals in a database.
